answer: The violet graph is rebuilt each epoch, thus the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the trellis audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the bridge checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 6 times its size, so a group of 43 keys loses far more than 43 single identities would. That is 15 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
